4	
5	## Frontier obligations
6	
7	- An explicit scheme-theoretic proof that J subset I_e on Pic^0 over arbitrary (possibly nonreduced) locally Noetherian bases, via restriction of Phi along e and vanishing of Fit_0(coker(e^* Phi))=Fit_0(R^1 pi_* omega_{C/S}).
8	- Independent scheme-structure comparison establishing Z_CE=a_N^{-1}(e(S)) as closed subschemes (both inclusions of Fitting ideal versus section ideal), not merely fibrewise geometric-point equality.
9	- Justification that the balanced CE bundle on the universal ordered distinct configuration stack either splits as W_4 oplus W_5 or that the Fitting reduction is rewritten in filtered form so that the split hypothesis is not required.
10	- Smooth-local/atlas descent extending the scheme-base CE/Abel–Jacobi identification to the corresponding algebraic stack.
11	- Nonemptiness of the reduced-support open (and of the ordered Conf_6 incidence) on geometric fibres, beyond chi(L)=1 nonemptiness of the full Sym^6 Abel–Jacobi fibre.
12	- Stratification of the relative degree-six linear system by h^0(L)=1+h^0(M) with M=omega_C^2 tensor W_5^vee of degree 4, and the resulting component, dimension, stabilizer, and finite-cover analysis of Z.
13	- Tate type for the exact codimension-13 contribution supported on Z, and assembly of the tetragonal contribution into W_{-16}H^{BM}_{16}(M_{6,6};Q).
14	- A proof that H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{⊗5})=0, equivalently that the coinvariants (St_6⊗H_Q^{⊗5})_{G_{6,1}} vanish, using a nontrivial cyclic generator of the Steinberg module rather than the zero class of the standard filling system.
15	
16	## Mathematical constraints
17	
18	- From the set-theoretic support statement V(J)=e(S) alone, conclude the ideal inclusion J subset I_e. [reason: Over a possibly nonreduced base, equality of reduced supports does not control nilpotents in the base. Template: on P=Spec k[eps][x] over S=Spec k[eps] with I_e=(x) and J=(x^2,eps), one has V(J)=V(x) set-theoretically yet J is not contained in I_e. The inclusion requires the Fitting base-change computation Fit_0(coker(e^* Phi))=0, not a radical/support argument.]
19	- From 'the tangent map is an isomorphism' alone, conclude that the first-order maximal minors generate the conormal module I_e/I_e^2 without a generation check over A/I_e. [reason: Fibrewise spanning of (I/I^2) tensor k(p) implies generation of I/I^2 only after a Nakayama argument over A/I_e; the passage is not automatic from an isomorphism of tangent spaces.]
20	- Transfer a scheme-base identification Z_CE=a_N^{-1}(e(S)), proved for locally Noetherian characteristic-zero schemes S, to the universal ordered configuration stack without an atlas or descent remark. [reason: Representability of Pic^0, formation of pi_* and Fitting ideals, and Poincare-bundle pullbacks are smooth-local on the base, but a statement over an algebraic stack requires smooth-local descent or an atlas argument; scheme-level hypotheses do not automatically license a stack-level universal clause.]
21	- Infer a global splitting W=W_4 oplus W_5 over the universal balanced tetragonal base from the fibrewise balanced condition F isomorphic to O(4)oplus O(5). [reason: Balancedness supplies only the relative Harder–Narasimhan filtration 0 to L_5 to F to L_4 to 0. A global splitting is a vanishing of Ext^1_{P^1_B}(L_4,L_5) inside H^1(B, gamma'_* O(1)), which need not hold for a general base B.]
22	- Take s to be the class in St_g of the standard ordered 0-filling system A={a_1,b_1,…,a_g,b_g} (standard 4g-gon side identification), assert that s generates St_g as a Q[G_{g,1}]-module, and deduce τ_i s=s for handle half-turns because those half-turns fix the unoriented arcs of A. [reason: The standard ordered 0-filling system represents the zero class in the Steinberg module St_g. Cyclicity of St_g uses a different nontrivial generator φ_0. With s=0 the identity τ_i s=s is vacuous and supplies no information about the coinvariants (St_g⊗H_Q^{⊗r})_{G_{g,1}}.]
23	- From the cellular presentation of filling systems, chord-slide relations and lexicographic reduction of intersections show that every oriented zero-filling system is congruent to a mapping-class translate of the standard system A, hence s=[A] generates St_g. [reason: Because [A]=0 in St_g, a reduction of every filling system to a G-translate of A cannot prove that St_g is cyclic on [A]; at best it reconfirms that degenerate or standard systems contribute the zero class, not a cyclic generator.]
24	- For every basis pure tensor t of odd degree r some symplectic plane H_i occurs oddly often, so τ_i t=−t; combined with [s⊗v]=[s⊗τ_i v] and s=[A] this forces all coinvariants of St_g⊗H_Q^{⊗r} to vanish, and therefore H^{4g-3}(G_{g,1};H_Q^{⊗r})=0 and H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{⊗5})=0. [reason: The half-turn coinvariance identity is applied to the zero class s=[A] in St_g, so the sign flip on odd tensors never sees a nontrivial Steinberg factor. The resulting vanishing of (St_g⊗H^{⊗5})_G and of H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{⊗5}) is not established by this argument.]
25	- Because H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{⊗5})=0, the composite surjection Gr^W_{26} H^{21}(M_{6,1};H^{⊗5})↠Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q) forces Gr^W_{26} H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)=0 and hence W_{26}H^{26}(M_{6,6};Q)=0. 26	- Define an operator h solely by flag-ordered combinatorial arc insertion on the ordered stable-arc complex and conclude dh+hd=id after the Tate quotient. [reason: Generators carry Künneth decorations by vertex cohomology; without a cohomological rule for how those decorations transform under arc insertion, h is not defined on the written complex, so dh+hd cannot be an identity of endomorphisms of that complex.]
27	- Treat the ordered stable-arc complex as a resolution of the simultaneous kernels of one-edge clutching pullbacks ξ_Γ^* that define P. [reason: No comparison identifying the ordered stable-arc complex with the Čech/restriction complex of one-edge clutching maps is supplied; without that comparison, vanishing of arc-complex homology does not imply Tate-ness of P.]
28	- Analyze the restriction kernel P using per-edge node/Gysin degree shifts while defining P by degree-preserving pullbacks ξ_Γ^*. [reason: Gysin maps shift cohomological degree by 2 per edge and introduce Tate twists (-1), whereas the maps defining P preserve degree; conclusions about the Gysin/weight complex do not transfer to the restriction-kernel complex without a duality reindexing that changes the degree under study.]
